answers.explanation: Five rows of 32 bits: 5 × 4 bytes = 20 bytes. Options can make it longer.
IHL counts 32-bit (4-byte) words, so 5 means 20 bytes and the maximum, 15, means 60 bytes.
1 is ICMP, 6 is TCP, 17 is UDP. The receiver uses this to hand the data to the right protocol.
Only the header. The data is protected by the transport layer's own checksum and, on each link, the frame's CRC.
TTL is a hop counter that stops packets looping forever. The router that drops it sends an ICMP Time Exceeded back to the source.
Changing any header field changes the checksum. You'll do exactly this in the Python exercise later in the chapter.
DF, Don't Fragment. If the datagram is too big for the next link and DF is set, the router drops it and reports back with ICMP.
Total length is the whole datagram. Subtract the header length (IHL × 4) to get the data size.
The type of service byte (today split into DSCP and ECN) marks the packet's class for scheduling.
